title: Patterned Wafer Inspection - Scratches Detection on Puma 9xxx
subtitle: Pre-Bonding Quality Validation for 3nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Yuki Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9xxx system to detect and classify Scratches defects during pre-bonding inspection at the 3nm technology node. The test is conducted at Pyeongtaek Fab 2 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Scratches defects that are critical to yield at the 3nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9xxx platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9xxx
- Inspection Type: Patterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Scratches
- Process Step: Pre-Bonding
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 3nm
- Fab Location: Pyeongtaek Fab 2

This test case applies to all Puma 9xxx systems deployed at Pyeongtaek Fab 2 for pre-bonding monitoring in the 3nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9xxx
Software Version: v14.6.130
Recipe: PATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_3nm_PRE_BONDING
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: High (156 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9xxx system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Patterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Scratches defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 3nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 72 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 95% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.7% for Patterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.92 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-10-06
Wafers Tested: 10
Total Defects Found: 3489
Defect Density: 493.59 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.2%
Capture Rate: 91.3%
Test Duration: 83 minutes
System Uptime: 97.7%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9xxx demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Scratches at the 3nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Edge-zone defect detection showed improved performance compared to previous revision.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Scratches at 3nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
